expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
expectations.evidence: Opens: "Keep the 8% and keep it simple. But make the rules simple rather than the cut uniform. With 68% of opex in payroll, 'every cost centre cuts 8%' mostly means cutting the billable people who earn your revenue." Then: "It rewards padded budgets, punishes lean ones, and hides the trade-offs from the board."

expectations.text: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
expectations.evidence: Table: "'8% below 2026': actions needed 8.3 (11.4% of baseline)" vs "'8% below baseline': 5.8"; "Settle three things with the chair ...: Which of these two the board means. Whether the target is in-year or the exit run-rate. Whether the real objective is margin."

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
expectations.evidence: Lever register: contractors 1.5, IT and software 0.5, housing 0.3, lease cars 0.2, recruitment fees 0.35, discretionary 0.5 = "Non-payroll subtotal 3.4" run-rate; "Each 1% of extra price realisation is worth about EUR 0.7M of EBIT".

expectations.text: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
expectations.evidence: "A hiring freeze with a weekly 30-minute exception panel ... Backfill only ... billable roles with demand ... critical control and security roles. Natural turnover becomes the main payroll lever"; "Redeploy before any exit ... offer voluntary options"; protect list: "Training and certification (EUR 0.7M) ... Sales capacity backed by pipeline. Retention of a named key-talent group", "no cuts without an ExCo decision".

expectations.text: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
expectations.evidence: No leaders' pay, bonus or perk measure. Option C even proposes "A salary round 1 point below market drift" for staff without any leadership measure.

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
expectations.evidence: Lever register has base, run-rate, 2027, owner and timing/dependency, but no confidence per lever, and no concrete stop/wait list ("budget holders choose what to stop"). The in-year shortfall is stated ("delivers about 5% in-year") and Option C covers the larger target.

overall_quality.evidence: Strong, reconciled figures with a lever register, anti-gaming rules, a bench double-count warning, a correct Dutch timeline and a ready instruction to budget holders; no leaders-first measure, and Option C cuts staff pay below drift without touching leaders' pay.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked: CPB 3.8% cao / 4.4% loonvoet / 2.7% CPI; transition payment cap EUR 102,000 in 2026; WMCO with one-month wait unless unions agree; art. 25(6) WOR suspension; arts. 31-31a WOR budget information without advice right; Wet DBA enforcement resumed in 2025. Lever register sums to 5.75 run-rate and 3.7 in 2027.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill, reference files or internal jargon such as 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt sets a cost target with a thin but positive margin; no bad outcome is described.

best_insight.value: Anti-gaming rules (a saving counts only when the run-rate line is gone, deferrals reported as deferrals, no reclassification to cost of sales or capex) and the warning not to count the same bench twice for insourcing and non-backfill.
best_insight.evidence: Reply section 3 'Anti-gaming rules'; paper section 4 'Watch the bench'.

suggestions.assertion: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples; every reply opened against the flat cut. It does not discriminate. Consider requiring the 'efficient vs wasteful' point to be shown with the user's own numbers or an example.

suggestions.assertion: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten samples. A sharper version would require the no-job levers to be sized in money with a range and shown against the gap, and pricing/leakage kept separate from the opex figure.

No assertion checks in-year versus run-rate phasing of savings and one-off costs under Dutch process (works council advice, WMCO, notice periods). That drove most of the difference in financial soundness between samples.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
suggestions.reason: Compound assertion (amount, timing, owner, confidence, stop list, remaining gap). Several strong samples missed only one element; consider splitting it so partial structure is visible.

eval_feedback.overall: Very good CFO work that misses leaders first and two parts of the board structure.
